q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
By the oath of the Qur'aan, which is a Reminder.
v.s: Sād. By the Qur’ān containing reminder...
v.c: Ṣãd. By the Quran, full of reminders!

q: In fact, the Kuffaar are steeped in tribalism
(constantly opposing and disputing with the Muslims).
v.s: But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension.
v.c: ˹This is the truth,˺ yet the disbelievers are ˹entrenched˺ in arrogance and opposition.

q: (The Kuffaar should rather take a lesson from the punishment that came to previous nations of Kuffaar.)
How many were the nations that We destroyed before them! Those people cried out
but it was not the time for escape.
(No help reached them and they were all destroyed.)
v.s: How many a generation have We destroyed before them, and they [then] called out; but it was not a time for escape.
v.c: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was too late to escape.

q: (arguing instead that a Prophet ought to be an angel rather than a man). (Instead of accepting his message,)
The Kuffaar say, “He is a magician and a great liar.”
v.s: And they wonder that there has come to them a warner [i.e., Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)] from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, “This is a magician and a liar.
v.c: Now, the pagans are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, “This is a magician, a total liar!

q: into one god? This is indeed something strange!”
v.s: Has he made the gods [only] one God? Indeed, this is a curious thing."
v.c: Has he reduced ˹all˺ the gods to One God? Indeed, this is something totally astonishing.”

q: A group of their leaders passed saying, “Carry on
(with what you are doing without paying attention to what Rasulullaah ﷺ says),
Undoubtedly, there is some ulterior motive behind this.”
v.s: And the eminent among them went forth, [saying], "Continue, and be patient over [the defense of] your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended.
v.c: The chiefs among them went forth saying, “Carry on, and stand firm in devotion to your gods. Certainly this is just a scheme ˹for power˺.

q: “We have not heard about such a thing
in the other religions. This is
v.s: We have not heard of this in the latest religion. This is not but a fabrication.
v.c: We have never heard of this in the previous faith. This is nothing but a fabrication.

q: (when he is merely a human being)
they are in doubt concerning My revelation
have not yet tasted My punishment.
v.s: Has the message been revealed to him out of [all of] us?" Rather, they are in doubt about My message. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
v.c: Has the Reminder been revealed ˹only˺ to him out of ˹all of˺ us?” In fact, they are ˹only˺ in doubt of My ˹revealed˺ Reminder. In fact, ˹they do so because˺ they have not yet tasted My punishment.

q: possess the treasures of mercy that belong to your Rabb, the Mighty, the Benevolent?

(If they had control over Allaah's mercy, they would have the right to delegate the mantle of Nubuwwah to whoever they wished. However, since they have no control over it, they have no right to object to the appointment of the Ambiyaa.)
v.s: Or do they have the depositories of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
v.c: Or ˹is it because˺ they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.

q: Or does the kingdom of the heavens, the earth, and all between these belong to them
(giving them the right to object to Allaah's appointment of Ambiyaa ﵊)?

(leading to the heavens). (The fact that this is impossible makes it clear that they have no control over the heavens. It is therefore unbecoming of them to object to the appointment of the Ambiyaa ﵊)
v.s: Or is theirs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [any] ways of access.
v.c: Or ˹is it because˺ the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything in between belongs to them? Let them then climb their way ˹to heaven, if their claim is true˺.

q: there is an army of people who are from the defeated armies
(of the past). (Subsequently, the Kuffaar of Makkah were defeated at the Battle of Badr.)
v.s: [They are but] soldiers [who will be] defeated there among the companies [of disbelievers].
v.c: This is just another ˹enemy˺ force bound for defeat out there.

q: Before them, the nations of Nooh ﵊ rejected
(also among the past defeated nations who rejected the Prophethood and message of the Ambiyaa ﵊ who came to them were)

(he is referred to as “the lord of the stakes” because he used tent stakes to torture people and because his army was so large that a great mass of wooden stakes were used whenever his army set up camp)...
v.s: The people of Noah denied before them, and [the tribe of] ʿAad and Pharaoh, the owner of stakes,
v.c: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺, as did ’Âd, Pharaoh of the mighty structures,

q: ...and the Thamud, the people of Loot ﵊ and the people of Aykah. These were the
(all of whom were punished because of their kufr).
v.s: And [the tribe of] Thamūd and the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket [i.e., people of Madyan]. Those are the companies.
v.c: Thamûd, the people of Lot, and the residents of the Forest. These were ˹all˺ enemy forces.

q: All of them did nothing but reject the Rusul. Therefore, My punishment had to come
v.s: Each of them denied the messengers, so My penalty was justified.
v.c: Each rejected their messenger, so My punishment was justified.

q: are waiting only for a single shout
(let alone allowing them time to accept Imaan).
v.s: And these [disbelievers] await not but one blast [of the Horn]; for it there will be no delay.
v.c: These ˹pagans˺ are awaiting nothing but a single Blast that cannot be stopped.

v.s: And they say, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share [of the punishment] before the Day of Account."
v.c: They say ˹mockingly˺, “Our Lord! Hasten for us our share ˹of the punishment˺ before the Day of Reckoning.”

q: Be patient with all they say and remember Our slave Dawood ﵊, the strong
v.s: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to God].
v.c: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And remember Our servant, David, the man of strength. Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.

q: the mountains that would glorify Allaah
with him by evening and at daybreak.
v.s: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, exalting [God] in the [late] afternoon and [after] sunrise.
v.c: We truly subjected the mountains to hymn ˹Our praises˺ along with him in the evening and after sunrise.

q: We also placed the birds at his service, who all gathered together
(at his command when it was time to engage in Tasbeeh).
v.s: And the birds were assembled, all with him repeating [praises].
v.c: And ˹We subjected˺ the birds, flocking together. All turned to him ˹echoing his hymns˺.

q: We strengthened his kingdom and granted him wisdom and sound judgement
v.s: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech.
v.c: We strengthened his kingship, and gave him wisdom and sound judgment.

q: disputants reached you, when they jumped over the wall and entered his
v.s: And has there come to you the news of the adversaries, when they climbed over the wall of [his] prayer chamber -
v.c: Has the story of the two plaintiffs, who scaled the ˹wall of David’s˺ sanctuary, reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

q: in on Dawood ﵊, he became alarmed
(because they had not entered his home conventionally, causing him to fear that they may have come with sinister motives).
They said, “Do not be afraid. We are merely two disputants
(who want you to resolve our argument).
against the other, so judge between us with the truth. Do not be unjust towards us and guide us on to the straight path
(by directing us towards the correct course of action).”
v.s: When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them? They said, "Fear not. [We are] two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not exceed [it] and guide us to the sound path.
v.c: When they came into David’s presence, he was startled by them. They said, “Have no fear. ˹We are merely˺ two in a dispute: one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth—do not go beyond ˹it˺—and guide us to the right way.

q: “This is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, while I have only one ewe. He said, 'Give it to me!' and he has been harsh towards me in speech.”
v.s: Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; so he said, 'Entrust her to me,' and he overpowered me in speech."
v.c: This is my brother. He has ninety-nine sheep while I have ˹only˺ one. ˹Still˺ he asked me to give it up to him, overwhelming me with ˹his˺ argument.”

q: said, “He has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes. Indeed, there are many partners who transgress against each other, except for those who have Imaan and who do righteous deeds.
It occurred to Dawood ﵊ that We had tested him
(by presenting to him a case that appeared to be straightforward and which came from people who displayed great disrespect, causing him to neglect listening to both sides),
so he sought forgiveness from his Rabb, fell prostrate, and turned to Him in repentance.
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
v.s: [David] said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to God].
v.c: David ˹eventually˺ ruled, “He has definitely wronged you in demanding ˹to add˺ your sheep to his. And certainly many partners wrong each other, except those who believe and do good—but how few are they!” Then David realized that We had tested him so he asked for his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned ˹to Him in repentance˺.

q: So We forgave him for that
Undoubtedly, he has a close position to Us, and
v.s: So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
v.c: So We forgave that for him. And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!

m: for it will lead you astray
q: “O Dawood! Indeed, We have made you a deputy
(to ensure that Our commands are carried out),
so judge between people with the truth, and do not follow carnal passions which will mislead you from Allaah's path. Verily there shall be a severe punishment for those who deviate from
Allaah's path because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
v.s: [We said], "O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of God." Indeed, those who go astray from the way of God will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account.
v.c: ˹We instructed him:˺ “O David! We have surely made you an authority in the land, so judge between people with truth. And do not follow ˹your˺ desires or they will lead you astray from Allah’s Way. Surely those who go astray from Allah’s Way will suffer a severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning.”

q: We have not created the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two in vain
This is the false belief of the Kuffaar
(they think that they have no purpose in this world and therefore do as they please).
May the destruction of the Fire be for those who commit kufr.
v.s: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and that between them aimlessly. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
v.c: We have not created the heavens and earth and everything in between without purpose—as the disbelievers think. So woe to the disbelievers because of the Fire!

q: (apart from thinking that they have been created in vain)
(the Kuffaar reject Imaan because they think that on the Day of Qiyaamah)
those who have Imaan and who do righteous deeds like
those who spread corruption on earth? Or should
(they reject Imaan because they think that on the Day of Qiyaamah)
the pious ones like the sinners?
(It is inconceivable even to the Kuffaar that the good and the evil should be treated equally.)
v.s: Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land? Or should We treat those who fear God like the wicked?
v.c: Or should We treat those who believe and do good like those who make mischief throughout the land? Or should We treat the righteous like the wicked?

q: is a blessed Book that We have revealed to you
so that the people may ponder over its verses and so that the intelligent
(the advice and warnings that it contains).
v.s: [This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.
v.c: ˹This is˺ a blessed Book which We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ so that they may contemplate its verses, and people of reason may be mindful.

q: slave indeed! He was certainly most penitent
v.s: And to David We gave Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was one repeatedly turning back [to God].
v.c: And We blessed David with Solomon—what an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.

q: When pure-bred horses of the finest calibre were presented before him one evening
(for inspection). (However, he was so enamoured by them and became so engrossed in inspecting them, that he failed to realise that the sun had already set, causing him to miss his salaah.)
v.s: [Mention] when there were exhibited before him in the afternoon the poised [standing] racehorses.
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when the well-trained, swift horses were paraded before him in the evening.

q: He said, “Indeed, I have given preference to the wealth of this world
over the remembrance of my Rabb
v.s: And he said, "Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good [things] over the remembrance of my Lord until it [i.e., the sun] disappeared into the curtain [of darkness]."
v.c: He then proclaimed, “I am truly in love with ˹these˺ fine things out of remembrance for Allah,” until they went out of sight.

q: to me.” He then began to strike their legs and manes

(their necks with his sword, thereby slaughtering them all. He did this as an offering to Allaah to make amends for his mistake. Since eating horses was permissible in his Shari'ah, he fed the meat to the people).
v.s: [He said], "Return them to me," and set about striking [their] legs and necks.
v.c: ˹He ordered,˺ “Bring them back to me!” Then he began to rub down their legs and necks.

q: body on his throne, after which he turned

(to Us in repentance). (The Ahadeeth do not explicitly mention any incident to which this verse refers. It is however possible that it refers to a narration mentioned in Bukhari. The narration states that Sulaymaan ﵊ once resolved to cohabit with each of his seventy wives on a certain night, intending to father a dynamic horseman from each wife, all of whom would be warriors in Jihaad. An angel who was with him advised him to say “Inshaa Allaah” (If Allaah wills”). Although he knew within his heart that everything occurs only with Allaah's will, he did not say the words. It then transpired that only one of the wives conceived. She finally bore deformed foetus, which lacked half of its torso. After narrating the story, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, “If Sulaymaan ﵊ had said, defiance 'Inshaa Allaah', he would have fat he red seventy youth who would have all fought in Jihaad.” If it is this narration that is referred to in the verse, the malformed foetus is referred to as the “body” cast on his throne.)
v.s: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he returned.
v.c: And indeed, We tested Solomon, placing a ˹deformed˺ body on his throne, then he turned ˹to Allah in repentance˺.

q: said, “O my Rabb! Forgive me and grant
me a kingdom that cannot be had by any other after me. Undoubtedly, You are the Great Giver.”
v.s: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
v.c: He prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me, and grant me an authority that will never be matched by anyone after me. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.”

q: the wind at his service, which would blow gently by his command
v.s: So We subjected to him the wind blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed,
v.c: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently at his command to wherever he pleased.

q: (They dived for pearls and constructed large buildings for him, as mentioned in verse 13 of Surah 34.)
v.s: And [also] the devils [of jinn] - every builder and diver.
v.c: And ˹We subjected to him˺ every builder and diver of the jinn,

q: there were others who were shackled
(for disobeying Sulaymaan ﵊ and for committing other crimes).
v.s: And others bound together in shackles.
v.c: and others bound together in chains.

q: (After giving Sulaymaan ﵊ all these favours, Allaah addressed him saying,)
(for you have complete control over your wealth with no one to answer to).'
v.s: [We said], "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account."
v.c: ˹Allah said,˺ “This is Our gift, so give or withhold ˹as you wish˺, never to be called to account.”

q: has a close position to Us, and
v.s: And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
v.c: And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!

q: (he was suffering from a severe disease after losing all his wealth and children)
he called his Rabb saying, “Verily Shaytaan has afflicted me with pain and difficulty
(by continuously trying to cast evil thoughts in my mind and by trying to mislead my wife as is mentioned in verse 44 ahead).'
v.s: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."
v.c: And remember Our servant Job, when he cried out to his Lord, “Satan has afflicted me with distress and suffering.”

m: (is a spring of) water to bathe
q: (When Allaah intended to cure him from the disease, Allaah addressed him saying,)
(When he did as commanded, Allaah caused a spring to gush forth from the ground. Allaah then said to him,)
This is cool water for bathing and drinking
(after which you will be cured from the disease).”
v.s: [So he was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for a] cool bath and drink."
v.c: ˹We responded,˺ “Stomp your foot: ˹now˺ here is a cool ˹and refreshing˺ spring for washing and drinking.”

q: We gifted him with his family and as many of them in addition
as a mercy from Us and a reminder for people of intelligence
(to remind them that Allaah rewards the patient ones and restores their losses).
v.s: And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
v.c: And We gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and a lesson for people of reason.

q: (Shaytaan once passed by the wife of Ayyoob ﵊ in the disguise of a physician. When she requested him to treat her husband, Shaytaan said, “I shall cure him without charging you for the treatment and medicines. However, when he is cured, I want you to say that I cured him.” She accepted. When she mentioned this to Ayyoob ﵊, he became angry because accepting the condition of treatment entailed uttering words of Shirk since Allaah is the only One Who can cure. He therefore took an oath to cane her a hundred times when he regained his strength. When Allaah cured him, the time came to fulfil his oath to cane her. It was then that Allaah advised him how he should fulfil his oath. Because she had loyally served Ayyoob ﵊' for many years, Allaah told him,)
do not breach your oath.” Verily, We found him
What a fine slave! He was certainly penitent.
v.s: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to God].
v.c: ˹And We said to him,˺ “Take in your hand a bundle of grass, and strike ˹your wife˺ with it, and do not break your oath.” We truly found him patient. What an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.

q: Our slaves Ibraheem ﵊, Is'haaq ﵊ and Ya'qoob ﵊, who were men of strength
(intelligent and possessing keen judgement in matters of Deen).
v.s: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - those of strength and [religious] vision.
v.c: And remember Our servants: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the men of strength and insight.

q: them for the special purpose of remembering the Aakhirah
(at all times so that they never lost sight of their duties to Allaah).
v.s: Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the home [of the Hereafter].
v.c: We truly chose them for the honour of proclaiming the Hereafter.

q: Undoubtedly, they are from among the chosen best
v.s: And indeed they are, to Us, among the chosen and outstanding.
v.c: And in Our sight they are truly among the chosen and the finest.

q: and Dhul Kifl ﵊. They were all from the very best
v.s: And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding.
v.c: Also remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Ⱬul-Kifl. All are among the best.

q: Without doubt, those with Taqwa will have a pleasant abode...
v.s: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return -
v.c: This is ˹all˺ a reminder. And the righteous will certainly have an honourable destination:

q: eternal Jannaat, with the doors opened for them
v.s: Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors will be opened to them.
v.c: the Gardens of Eternity, whose gates will be open for them.

q: They will recline there, asking for
the abundance of fruit and drinks.
v.s: Reclining within them, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink.
v.c: There they will recline, calling for abundant fruit and drink.

q: They shall have with them wives
v.s: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances and of equal age.
v.c: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and equal age.

q: “This is what you have been promised for the Day of Reckoning.”
v.s: This is what you, [the righteous], are promised for the Day of Account.
v.c: This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.

q: “Indeed, this is Our provision, which will never come to an end
(so you need never fear losing it).”
v.s: Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no depletion.
v.c: This is indeed Our provision that will never end.

q: (so understand well that you have to accept Imaan and do good to achieve it).
As for the rebellious, theirs shall be the worst of abodes.
v.s: This [is so]. But indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return -
v.c: That is that. And the transgressors will certainly have the worst destination:

q: Jahannam. What a terrible resting place indeed!
v.s: Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the resting place.
v.c: Hell, where they will burn. What an evil place to rest!

q: so taste it! This is the boiling water and Ghassaaq...
(pus of the people of hell mixed with the poison of snakes and scorpions)'
v.s: This - so let them taste it - is scalding water and [foul] purulence.
v.c: Let them then taste this: boiling water and ˹oozing˺ pus,

q: “...and a multitude of other punishments of its
v.s: And other [punishments] of its type [in various] kinds.
v.c: and other torments of the same sort!

q: (Since many groups will be entered into Jahannam in succession, those who entered first will tell each other as they watch the others entering,)
with you. There is no welcome for them. They shall certainly be entered into the Fire
(just as we have been. We can therefore expect no assistance from them).”
v.s: [Its inhabitants will say], "This is a company bursting in with you. No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire."
v.c: ˹The misleaders will say to one another,˺ “Here is a crowd ˹of followers˺ being thrown in with us. They are not welcome, ˹for˺ they ˹too˺ will burn in the Fire.”

q: will say, “No! You are the ones for whom there is no welcome! You people have brought this
v.s: They will say, "Nor you! No welcome for you. You, [our leaders], brought this upon us, and wretched is the settlement."
v.c: The followers will respond, “No! You are not welcome! You brought this upon us. What an evil place for settlement!”

q: “O our Rabb! Double the punishment in the Fire for those who have brought this
v.s: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase for him double punishment in the Fire."
v.c: Adding, “Our Lord! Whoever brought this upon us, double their punishment in the Fire.”

q: (In addition to cursing those who misled them,)
will say, “Why do we not see
men whom we regarded as evil people
(in the world, thinking that they had been misled)?”
v.s: And they will say, "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst?
v.c: The tyrants will ask ˹one another˺, “But why do we not see those we considered to be lowly?

q: (when they had been deserving of Jannah),
(The fact is that they will never see the Mu'mineen because the Mu'mineen will be in Jannah.)
v.s: Is it [because] we took them in ridicule, or has [our] vision turned away from them?"
v.c: Were we wrong in mocking them ˹in the world˺? Or do our eyes ˹just˺ fail to see them ˹in the Fire˺?”

q: of the people of the Fire.
v.s: Indeed, that is truth [i.e., reality] - the quarreling of the people of the Fire.
v.c: This dispute between the residents of the Fire will certainly come to pass.

q: (to the people), “(If you reject my message, no harm will come to me because)
I am but a Warner, and there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, the One, the Omnipotent.”
(Your rejection will harm only yourselves because Allaah certainly has the power to punish you.)
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except God, the One, the Prevailing,
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a warner. And there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah—the One, the Supreme.

q: “He is the Rabb of the heavens, the earth, and whatever is between the two. He is the Mighty,
(Who will forgive you if you accept Imaan).”
v.s: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver."
v.c: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between—the Almighty, Most Forgiving.”

q: (message of Towheed and the injunctions of the Shari'ah that I am conveying to you)
v.s: Say, "It is great news
v.c: Say, “This ˹Quran˺ is momentous news,

v.s: From which you turn away.
v.c: from which you ˹pagans˺ are turning away.”

q: “I have no knowledge of lofty chiefs
(with Allaah concerning the creation of Aadam ﵊, as mentioned in verses 30-33 of Surah 2).” (However, I can inform you of this because, Allaah reveals it to me as a Nabi.)
v.s: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly [of angels] when they were disputing [the creation of Adam].
v.c: ˹And say,˺ “I had no knowledge of the highest assembly ˹in heaven˺ when they differed ˹concerning Adam˺.

q: only because I am a clear warner
(a Nabi who warns you about the consequences of rejecting Imaan).”
v.s: It has not been revealed to me except that I am a clear warner."
v.c: What is revealed to me is that I am only sent with a clear warning.”

q: When your Rabb said to the angels, “Verily, I am creating a human
v.s: [So mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay.
v.c: ˹Remember, O Prophet˺ when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to create a human being from clay.

q: shaped him and blown My spirit
into him, then every one of you should bow down to him.”
v.s: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration."
v.c: So when I have fashioned him and had a spirit of My Own ˹creation˺ breathed into him, fall down in prostration to him.”

q: (when Allaah issued the command to bow down)
every one of the angels bowed down to him...
v.s: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely,
v.c: So the angels prostrated all together—

q: ...except Iblees. He was haughty, and was from those who rejected
v.s: Except Iblees; he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers.
v.c: but not Iblîs, who acted arrogantly, becoming unfaithful.

q: said, “O Iblees! What has prevented you from prostrating to what I have created with My own hands? Are you too proud, or are you
v.s: [God] said, "O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant [then], or were you [already] among the haughty?"
v.c: Allah asked, “O Iblîs! What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Own Hands? Did you ˹just˺ become proud? Or have you always been arrogant?”

q: replied, “I am better than he. You have created me from fire, while you have created him from clay.”

(While Iblees argued that fire is better than clay because fire burns upwards and clay falls down, he failed to realise that clay extinguishes fire and that it is constructive whereas fire is destructive.)
v.s: He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
v.c: He replied, “I am better than he is: You created me from fire and him from clay.”

q: for you are certainly an outcast
v.s: [God] said, "Then get out of it [i.e., Paradise], for indeed, you are expelled.
v.c: Allah commanded, “Then get out of Paradise, for you are truly cursed.

q: “My curse shall be on you until the Day of Reckoning.”
v.s: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense."
v.c: And surely upon you is My condemnation until the Day of Judgment.”

q: said, “O my Rabb! Grant me respite
(just before the blowing of the Trumpet).”
v.s: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
v.c: Satan appealed, “My Lord! Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection.”

q: said, “You are then from those given respite...”
v.s: [God] said, "So indeed, you are of those reprieved
v.c: Allah said, “You will be delayed

q: “...until the Day of the appointed time
v.s: Until the Day of the time well-known."
v.c: until the appointed Day.”

q: By Your honour! I shall definitely mislead
v.s: [Iblees] said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.
v.c: Satan said, “By Your Glory! I will certainly mislead them all,

v.s: Except, among them, Your chosen servants."
v.c: except Your chosen servants among them.”

q: declared, “I speak the truth, and it is the truth that I always speak.”
v.s: [God] said, "The truth [is My oath], and the truth I say -
v.c: Allah concluded, “The truth is—and I ˹only˺ say the truth—:

q: “I shall certainly fill Jahannam with you and with all those of them
v.s: [That] I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them that follow you all together."
v.c: I will surely fill up Hell with you and whoever follows you from among them, all together.”

q: “I do not ask you people for any payment for this
and I am not among those who pretend.”
(I am not one of those who would lay a false claim to prophethood, neither would! I claim that the Qur'aan is from Allaah if it were not.)
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “I do not ask you for it [i.e., the Qur’ān] any payment, and I am not of the pretentious.
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹Quran˺, nor do I pretend to be someone I am not.

q: (Qur'aan is certainly from Allaah and it)
v.s: It is but a reminder to the worlds.
v.c: It is only a reminder to the whole world.

q: (However, if you refuse to accept the truth of the Qur'aan,)
You will surely become aware of the reality
v.s: And you will surely know [the truth of] its information after a time."
v.c: And you will certainly know its truth before long.”
